questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Switzerland?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Switzerland article.

questions.proof: Switzerland does not have an official capital city, but Bern is used as though it is the capital.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Switzerland?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Languages” part of the Switzerland article.

questions.proof: There are four official languages in Switzerland: German, French, Italian, and Romansh.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “East of Switzerland are _____ and Liechtenstein.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Switzerland”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Switzerland article.

questions.proof: East of Switzerland are Austria and Liechtenstein.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “However, on February 28, 2022 Switzerland joined the imposition of economic sanctions against _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “against”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Switzerland article.

questions.proof: However, on February 28, 2022 Switzerland joined the imposition of economic sanctions against Russia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Most Swiss literature was written in German from _____ until 1798.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the thirteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Literature” part of the Switzerland article.

questions.proof: Most Swiss literature was written in German from 1291 until 1798.
